Why it exists

Retail algo trading usually goes one of two ways: backtests that never meet a real market, or live bots that trade before anyone has checked the numbers. Smart Trader is a zero-cost platform that does the boring part first: it backtests every strategy, picks the best one per stock, and watches the live market for setups.

The newer work closes the loop. A heavily guarded adapter places real orders on Dhan for a short whitelist, so real fills can be compared with what the simulator predicted.

How it works

What happens between the first click and the result.

  1. 1

    Backtest

    The Python engine runs strategies over NSE price history and saves a report for each stock.

  2. 2

    Activate

    A stock, strategy and timeframe that earned it goes on the active list; that list is all the scanner watches.

  3. 3

    Scan the market

    During market hours the scanner manages open positions and trailing stops, then looks for new setups between 09:30 and the 15:10 square-off.

  4. 4

    Signal

    Each signal is saved with a simulated trade and pushed to the dashboard over WebSocket and to Telegram.

  5. 5

    Execute, carefully

    For a whitelisted pair, a market order goes to Dhan and a broker-side protective stop is placed immediately.

What it does

The parts that make Smart Trader different.

  • Strategy library with a backtester

    31 strategies, intraday and swing, each backtested before it ever sees live data.

  • Live scanner and alerts

    Entries, trailing stops and exits handled in market hours, with WebSocket and Telegram alerts.

  • Charts, portfolio and risk

    Candlestick charting with portfolio and risk tracking in a React dashboard.

  • Guarded real-money execution

    Fixed 2% risk per trade, a ₹600 daily-loss kill switch, 20 orders a day, and stops that live at the broker.

Under the hood

How the pieces connect, and the engineering calls behind them.

  1. NSE price history
  2. Python engine + backtester
  3. Live scanner
  4. NestJS API + Postgres
  5. WebSocket + Telegram
  6. React dashboard
  7. Dhan (guarded)

Design decisions

  • Risk is fixed, size flexes

    Real position size is the smaller of a risk-based, a notional and a hard quantity cap, so risk stays at 2% whatever the stop distance.

  • Stops live at the broker

    A protective stop-limit rests at Dhan from the first second, so a crash on my side can't leave a position unprotected.

  • State survives restarts

    Positions and the kill switch are stored and reconciled with the broker on boot, after an in-memory map once lost a live position.

  • Fails safe

    If the static-IP proxy that SEBI rules require goes down, orders fail; they never bypass it.

Honest limits

Where it stands today, without the polish.

  • Real-money trading is at an early validation stage on a small account. It is not a proven autonomous system.
  • Real execution is cash-equity intraday only, and exits can lag the market by up to about 100 seconds.
  • Paper results are before real costs, so live net returns will trail the simulation.

Questions

Can I use it?

The app is private. The source is public on GitHub if you'd like to read how it works.

Does it trade real money?

Yes, narrowly: two whitelisted intraday pairs on a small, supervised account. Everything else is simulated.

Is this investment advice?

No. It's an engineering project, and its own docs say not to treat it as a proven system.
